title: Arithmetic Operators
instructions: C does math with these symbols: + add, - subtract, * multiply, / divide, and % remainder.
Watch out: dividing two ints CHOPS the answer. 7 / 2 gives 3, not 3.5, because ints can't hold a decimal.
The % operator gives the remainder (what's left over). 7 % 2 is 1.
Want a real decimal answer? Use doubles instead of ints.
To print an actual % sign with printf, write %% (two of them).
task: Add the line that prints the remainder of a divided by b, so the output ends with:  a %% b = 1
hint:
Use the % operator, and %% to print a literal percent sign:

    printf("a %% b = %d\n", a % b);
expected_output:
a + b = 9
a / b = 3
a % b = 1
